question: Whose burden is naming, if customary karma conceals the enjoyer giving inferior enjoyment?
premises: action, that world-customary indeed, giving inferior enjoyment
inference: Customary inferior-enjoyment karma hides the enjoyer; naming it is no burden of ours.
uncertainties: loka-rudha reading kept per gloss; independent verification pending
plain_english: Action, that world-customary indeed, giving inferior enjoyment, conceals enjoyer-form — of designation, but not our burden.
